Nice to see $DPZ moving up a little bit. I've been enjoying their Pizza a little lately, with the second child now here. No dishes = V Nice. Often pair with a michelada which i make using a non-alcoholic Corona. True $STZ baggy till death. At the end of the year its often good to just sell off losers, but the big exception, at least for me, is that if they do lots of buybacks, you keep those ones. If you have two positions you like equally at the end of the year, and they are down equally, but one issuances shares for growth or just to pay their employees, and the other is pecuniary with its stock and buys back a lot, it seems to make sense to rotate the issuer into the one that buys back stock. So, holding $STZ into '26 even though it didn't really work out so far.

We will see how $GTLB does tomorrow after it sold off after earnings. 25% growth and continued margin expansion seemed pretty solid but I guess the market wanted more? $GTLB has been something of an experiment for me. Normally I would never buy a software stock at such a high price sales. All my big wins in software have been buying at 3-4x price/sales.

Buying at high price/sales can work ok - if you pay 10x p/s for something growing 30% a year, and it keeps up that growth for 5 years and then you sell it for 10x p/s, thats a 2.7x, pretty solid result with no multiple expansion. The key bet you're making here to make this work is that the growth will not decay. If it does, you will have a problem, because you will have decaying growth and also multiple compression. Not great. This is what's happened with a lot of software stocks lately ($MNDY for example).

But if you buy something growing 20% a year when you buy it at 4x price sales, but it instead beats and grows 30% a year, not only will you get the 270% return from 5 years of 30% growth, but you will also get another ~100% on top since the multiple will surely expand 6-10x sales. This is a dramatically better return than situation 1, not just a little bit better.

Anyway, just a late night thought as i ponder the Git.

Not a lot of changes over the last week, just some modest year end shuffling. I did get torched with the $TNA short into rate cuts - maybe was avoidable, need to think about that a bit more. In general, the current strategy is just to assume that if its worth picking individual stocks, you can outperform IWM/TNA significantly, so you should up gross leverage and short TNA. That said, i'd prefer to just be short more individiual stocks which tends to go better - but haven't been putting in the time to manage more than the current book.

Looks like eventually we are going to get even with $STZ (might already be with a dividend, pretty close), I am doing my part drinking plenty of non-alcoholic Coronas. Interestingly, my wife has taken a liking to them too, with 0 prodding. Perhaps non-alcoholic is actually an order of magnitude larger business than we all think. Growing super fast at the moment, but the exact final TAM still remains very much an open question.

Mostly working on Japan, Korea and thinking about AI winners/losers at the moment, but nothing to report really, just looking for the next major thing to focus on in 2026.. I do need to dedicate some thinking to whether or not it makes sense for Anthropic to eventually buy GitLab. It seems like at this point Amazon is going to pass, but it would make a tonne of sense for Anthropic to own it, and i am a mega Anthropic bull, i think they will have the money to do it.

Unlike OpenAI, who i think should buy Box or DropBox with stock (but might have trouble doing so at a 500b+ valuation, and also might have trouble borrowing money), i think Anthropic could get more cash to buy a high revenue business like GTLB pretty easily - their core business is so much tighter and more focused, which makes it much less risky to lend them the money to do this, or for shareholders to take stock. Perhaps something like this would happen post IPO... Need to ponder more, but would be a major $GTLB bull case.

Did I sell $ISSC despite it being a high conviction (10%) position that I felt strongly would hit full capacity at its Greenville NC on its F16 program, but not until 2026? Yes.

I figured I would rotate into something else and rebuy after earnings were flat or declining in Q4 (they were) with a bulk of growth coming in '26.

But looks like market gets it now and i'm priced out of a bunch of work i did, my model is pretty exhaustive... in theory if you have a few positions you like equally it is just rational, but I think with limited time to research might just need a significantly higher bar to sell things that have been written up. Results oriented, but pretty sure the data I have is starting to tell me if i've done a lot of work on something and position it fairly large, it usually does work out and shouldn't try to do clever stuff.

Interestingly the most recent price run up going into earnings is probably from this $LMT release about the Greenville program: https://t.co/LThidgWkub. So there were some clever buyers that have connected the two things I think.

SoftBank is rushing to deliver $22.5B to OpenAI.

The deal was set up in April 2025, with later payments tied to OpenAI completing a for-profit transition by year-end, which sources say it achieved by October 2025.

To raise cash quickly, SoftBank has sold its full Nvidia stake and cut down its T-Mobile position, while also tightening approvals inside its Vision Fund to focus resources on the OpenAI payment.

Another lever is borrowing, because SoftBank can draw margin loans backed by Arm shares after expanding undrawn capacity, and it can also use cash, bonds, or bridge loans.

PayPay’s planned initial public offering (IPO) is another path, but it slipped into 2026Q1 after a 43-day U.S. government shutdown that ended in November.

OpenAI is burning cash on training and inference, meaning the cost of running models for answers, and it is also funding giant buildouts like Stargate that bundle chips, power, cooling, and servers.

Sam Altman has said OpenAI is targeting 30GW of compute for about $1.4T, with a long-run goal of adding 1GW per week, even though 1GW can cost more than $40B today.

---

reuters. com/business/media-telecom/softbank-races-fulfill-225-billion-funding-commitment-openai-by-year-end-sources-2025-12-19/
